The only candidate, M9, is a decision gateway ("Have all required items?") that the description never states. The description says only that some items are owned, some may be borrowed or bought cheaply from friends, and the rest are bought. A guideline would have to invent an all-items-available check, and documented QA-04 says to remove unsupported elements and keep only stated alternatives. M14, M19 and M20 also point to elements the description does not contain. The reference therefore adds structure the description does not support, so no guideline can be grounded in these records. rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description splits the required items into ones the actor already has and ones the actor must still obtain, and the following steps depend on whether the full set is available: After the task that establishes which required items are already held, model an exclusive decision gateway that asks whether the full set of required items is available. Route the branch where items are still missing to the task or tasks that obtain them, and route the branch where the full set is available onward to the next step. Do not leave this check implicit in a list task or in the first step that follows it.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description splits the required items into ones the actor already has and ones the actor must still obtain, and the following steps depend on whether the full set is available

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that an external system gives the user several separate lists or sets of alternatives (for example items to gather and options to choose from), each introduced as its own output of that system: Model each separately stated list or set as its own task, labeled with the verb and object the description uses for the system providing it, followed by the object of that set. Do not merge different lists, or the choices attached to them, into one receiving task. The user's later action on a list (checking, choosing, buying) remains a separate task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that an external system gives the user several separate lists or sets of alternatives (for example items to gather and options to choose from), each introduced as its own output of that system

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that two or more activities or branches may run at the same time with no required order, and a later step is described as starting only after all of them are finished (or as needing their results); a branch may also state that some of its work must be repeated a minimum number of times: Open the concurrent branches with a parallel gateway, with one outgoing flow per branch, and close them with a parallel gateway (join) before the dependent step, so the later step waits for all branches. If a branch must repeat its work a stated minimum number of times, model that work as a task inside a loop: an exclusive gateway after the task returns the flow to the task until the minimum count is reached, then passes it on. Add no conditions to the fork or join flows, and do not replace the join with an exclusive gateway.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that a party receives several kinds of information at once and then performs several separate activities on them, with no order stated between those activities, and a later step follows the work

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names a work activity with its own verb and object, and a generated task label would use a different verb, a synonym, a restated object, or extra words such as a recipient, a reaction, or a circumstance that the description does not attach to that activity's own action: Label the task with the verb and object words that the description uses for that activity, in the same order and without synonyms or added qualifiers. Model any circumstance, reaction, or recipient that the description states separately as an event, a gateway branch, or the sequence flow leading to the task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names a work activity with its own verb and object, and a generated task label for that activity adds a receipt verb, a qualifier, a circumstance or an extra object that the description does not attach to that activity's own action
